name: review
description: Run a scoped diff review and file prioritized inline suggestions.
author: Localix

commands.name: review
commands.description: Review code changes and file inline fixes — pick a scope (working · staged · unstaged · branch · commit · pr).

args.name: scope
args.description: What to review. Omit for the uncommitted working tree.

options.description: All uncommitted changes (staged + unstaged) — the default
Every commit on this branch vs its base
A specific commit — picked from the list or typed as any ref (e.g. HEAD~2 or a sha)
A GitHub pull request — picked from the open-PR list or typed as its number

args.name: branch
args.description: Pick a branch to review vs its base (live list); or type any branch name.

args.name: commit
args.description: Pick a recent commit to review (live list); or type any ref (HEAD~2, a sha, a tag).

args.name: pr
args.description: Pick an open GitHub pull request (live list via gh); or type its number.

args.name: focus
args.description: Optional: a specific concern to prioritize.

commands.prompt:
You are coordinating a code review. Do NOT review the code on this turn and do NOT read files — your ONLY job is to start one review fork and relay what it reports.

Review scope: ${scope}
Focus (optional): ${focus}

If a git resource was attached to this message, its diff appears in an attached context block above. That attached diff IS the review target — put it in the task and require the fork to review exactly that, ignoring the scope below.

Otherwise resolve the scope into a diff target for the task:
- blank or `working` → all uncommitted changes (staged + unstaged)
- `staged` → staged changes only
- `unstaged` → unstaged working-tree changes only
- `branch` → the branch `${branch}` (the branch picked/typed; if empty, the current branch) vs its merge-base with the upstream/main
- `commit` → the single commit `${commit}` (the ref picked/typed for the commit arg; if empty, review `HEAD`)
- `pr` → the GitHub pull request `${pr}` (the PR picked/typed; via the `gh` CLI)

Start the review as a fork of yourself: call `fork` with `title: "Code review"` and a `task` that carries the resolved scope (and, when a diff was attached above, that diff verbatim so the fork reviews exactly it), the optional focus, and this procedure: gather the diff per file, never as one whole-repository dump; read only the enclosing context a hunk needs; run nothing that edits files, builds or tests; report only issues this diff introduced, each with a severity (P0 drop everything, P1 urgent bug, P2 should fix, P3 minor), a file:line anchor, the triggering scenario and a concrete fix; and end the final report with a fenced ```json verdict block — {"verdict": "pass|fail|comment", "summary", "findings": [{"severity", "title", "file", "line"}]} — as the very last thing. If `fork` is unavailable here, say so and do not claim that a review started. The fork runs in the BACKGROUND: tell the user the review is underway and END your turn — do not poll or wait. When its report arrives as a follow-up message, write a short summary ONLY — counts by severity and the headline issues — never re-list every comment. Take the verdict, counts and headline issues from the report's ```json verdict block; if the block is missing or malformed, fall back to the prose report. If it found nothing, say so plainly.
